So, I know a lot of you don't carry spare mags, but I've always done so, due to "tap-rack-bang" training to clear any problems.

If you also carry a backup, how do you carry it? Is there a better way you wish you could carry it? How do you wish you could change it?
How do you carry your spare magazines?

I'll start:

I carry mine in my left cargo pocket. It's not the best, but it doesn't fall out and it doesn't print. I also don't have to worry about if it's a single-stack or a double-stack mag... they all fit the same in a cargo pocket.

The downside is that grabbing it out of my pocket is less than ideal, and takes some time. I wish I could do something IWB, but I haven't been able to find a great magazine holster. I guess I've been spoiled by my crossbreed (regular gun holster), and I'm just unhappy with everything I've seen in the magazine area... anyone have any suggestions?

I do not carry a spare magazine, generally.

If I have cargo pants or a big coat with an inside pocket, I might toss it in there but otherwise I don't bother.

I'll be interested to see the other replies here.

OWB mag carriers. They keep them in the same place with the same alignment all the time. There's no perfect solution, so I just wind up dressing to conceal everything.

The backup, at present, is a Smith & Wesson J frame. I need a good holster for it, though. All I have right now are cheap ones that don't do a great job.
Any suggestions on OWB carriers? All of the ones I've tried have "holes" like a Leatherman sheath that can show what you're carrying... which isn't what I am looking for.
The one I have for my current carry pistol is from Blade-Tech. Kydex, adjustable tension, adjustable positioning. Double stack mags are thick enough to print pretty well, though.
I pretty much just leave them on the coffee table.
I have an upper body elastic conceal holster with a slot for a mag. It's fairly comfortable and hides both pistol (has room for two) and mag well. Made by Galco

I've seen those, and have something like it. I use mine when I'm in a suit, but it's hard to conceal anything in a T-shirt. It also makes it difficult to get to your weapon/mag through a T-shirt.

Works GREAT in a button-up and a blazer, though.
Yes it is much harder to get to, I typically only use it when I want the extra mag, all day hikes for example. I carry an M&P .40 with 10+1 loaded so the need for the mag doesn't come around often.

The general rule of thumb for automatics is to carry on the opposite side, however you do it. This is just another reason to love shoulder rigs. A belly pack is the only time magazines are combined with the gun. I don't use front pockets in case I need to reload while sitting or crouching, but otherwise it's as needs dictate. I keep my pockets empty and I haven't yet had an issue with lint, so I don't use any magazine carriers in pockets.

Well, since I carry my weapon in an IWB holster, I've tried IWB/OWB magazine pouches. I've tried Leatherman pouches, dedicated magazine pouches, and a litany of other belt-based carry methods. Nothing seems to carry well, which is why I carry in a cargo pocket.

I think if you can just drop them in your pocket depends on the magazine too. Glock seems not to care, either traditional fat G19 magsl or G42 singles. But I heard about Kahr magazines losing rounds in pockets. My own Kahr is a .45, so it does not suffer from it (uses 1911 magazines essentially).
